title: Senior Manager, Identity & Access Management
description:
Mylan Inc. Viatris is a global healthcare company uniquely positioned to bridge the traditional divide between generics and brands, combining the best of both to more holistically address healthcare needs globally. With a mission to empower people worldwide to live healthier at every stage of life, we provide access at scale, currently supplying high-quality medicines to approximately 1 billion patients around the world annually and touching all of life's moments, from birth to the end of life, acute conditions to chronic diseases.
We have been included on number of award lists that demonstrate the impact we are making.
Every day, we rise to the challenge to make a difference and here’s how the Senior Manager, Identity & Access Management will make an impact:
The primary purpose of the Senior Manager, Identity & Access Management (IAM), is to lead the strategy, delivery, and maturation of enterprise identity security capabilities across Viatris systems, applications, cloud environments, and privileged technology resources. The role defines and drives standardized, automated identity controls across authentication, privileged access, access governance, directory services, and identity lifecycle management. The role partners with Cybersecurity, IT, Cloud, Infrastructure, HR, and application teams to reduce fragmented and manual identity processes while strengthening a sustainable operating model for a foundational enterprise security capability. The role develops internal leadership depth through deliberate knowledge transfer, succession planning, and coaching while reducing security risk from inconsistent or excessive access and operational cost from decentralized identity-management practices.
Key responsibilities for this role include:

• Lead development and execution of the enterprise IAM strategy, roadmap, and capability maturity plan across authentication, privileged access, access governance, and identity lifecycle services.

• Set identity security architecture direction and implementation standards for workforce identities, privileged accounts, service accounts, application access, and cloud identity integrations.

• Define reusable IAM patterns, reference designs, control standards, and implementation approaches that enable secure and consistent identity adoption across enterprise platforms.

• Establish automated and policy-driven identity controls for joiner, mover, leaver, access request, access review, and privileged-access processes.

• Lead identity risk reviews, access governance assessments, and senior-level risk discussions for critical systems, privileged technology resources, and high-risk access scenarios.

• Define identity security assurance approaches that identify excessive access, orphaned accounts, privilege misuse, weak authentication, and lifecycle control gaps.

• Direct the use and maturation of IAM, IGA, PAM, directory, MFA, SSO, federation, and identity analytics capabilities to validate control effectiveness and drive remediation.

• Manage a portfolio of IAM programs from requirements through design, implementation, maturation, operational transition, and continual service improvement.

• Assess enterprise IAM capability gaps and sponsor practical implementation roadmaps with Cybersecurity, IT, Cloud, Infrastructure, HR, and application stakeholders.

• Drive adoption of automated, repeatable, and policy-driven IAM practices across access provisioning, deprovisioning, certification, privileged access, and authentication processes.

• Advise technology teams and Cybersecurity leadership on identity security priorities, risk tradeoffs, service improvements, platform investments, and operating model decisions.

• Lead, coach, and develop IAM professionals while establishing knowledge transfer, succession planning, and sustainable coverage for critical identity security capabilities.

• Develop cybersecurity countermeasures, identity risk mitigation approaches, and implementation guidance aligned

title: Maintenance Manager
description:
Position Summary Bennett Heat Treating & Brazing Co., Inc. is seeking an experienced and self-directed Maintenance Manager to oversee all production-equipment and facility-maintenance activities. Although the title is Maintenance Manager, this is an individual-contributor position with no direct reports. The successful candidate will personally troubleshoot, repair, inspect, and maintain electrical and mechanical systems throughout the facility. A strong Maintenance Technician or Maintenance Supervisor who is ready to assume full ownership of the maintenance function may be considered. This position works frequently with 480V electrical systems, DC voltage, water pumps, vacuum pumps, furnace elements, fans, hydraulics, and other industrial equipment. The Maintenance Manager will also maintain repair records, manage preventive maintenance activities, monitor MRO inventory, assist with quality and safety initiatives, and support corrective actions. The current maintenance workload is approximately 40% preventive maintenance and 60% emergency or corrective repair. A major objective of this position is to improve the established maintenance program and move the facility toward a more preventive and reliability-focused model.
Key Responsibilities Electrical Maintenance and Troubleshooting Diagnose, troubleshoot, and repair electrical failures affecting production and facility equipment. Work safely with electrical systems operating at up to 480V AC, as well as DC-voltage systems. Inspect electrical components, wiring, connections, motors, controls, switches, relays, contactors, heating elements, and related equipment. Use appropriate testing equipment to identify electrical faults. Replace defective electrical components according to applicable safety requirements. Identify recurring electrical failures and recommend permanent corrective actions. Report unsafe electrical conditions immediately. Coordinate specialized electrical work with qualified contractors when required. Maintain accurate documentation of electrical repairs and recurring problems. Electrical issues are currently the most common type of maintenance emergency within the facility. Mechanical Maintenance Troubleshoot and repair mechanical systems and production equipment. Maintain water pumps, vacuum pumps, furnace elements, fans, motors, hydraulic equipment, and related components. Inspect equipment for wear, vibration, leaks, overheating, unusual noise, and other signs of mechanical failure. Repair or replace defective bearings, seals, motors, belts, pumps, fans, valves, and mechanical components. Support alignment, adjustment, lubrication, and replacement activities. Evaluate whether equipment should be repaired, rebuilt, or replaced. Reduce repeat failures through root-cause analysis and corrective action. Maintain orderly tools, parts, and maintenance work areas. Vacuum Furnace Maintenance Perform routine and corrective maintenance on vacuum furnaces and related systems. Support the maintenance of vacuum pumps, heating elements, fans, controls, and supporting equipment. Investigate vacuum leaks, heating issues, electrical faults, and equipment-performance concerns. Coordinate furnace downtime and repairs with Operations and Production. Learn facility-specific furnace systems through company-provided on-site training. Maintain accurate records of furnace inspections, repairs, and preventive maintenance activities. Previous vacuum furnace experience is a strong advantage but is not required. The company will provide on-site training to a candidate with strong transferable electrical and mechanical skills. Preventive and Predictive Maintenance Maintain and improve the established preventive maintenance program. Schedule preventive maintenance according to equipment condition, manufacturer recommendations, usage, production priorities, and operational risk. Coordinate maintenance activities with Operations and Quality. Complete inspections, lubrication, adjustments
